content: Oral estrogen replacement therapy may necessitate higher doses of lonapegsomatropin. Close monitoring is recommended. Lopinavir can increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Loratadine may also increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, requiring caution and monitoring. Lorlatinib, on the other hand, decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative drugs should be considered. Lovastatin increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, necessitating caution and monitoring. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring close monitoring. Conjugated estrogens can reduce magnesium chloride levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage, though the clinical significance is unclear. Similar effects are observed with magnesium citrate, magnesium hydroxide, magnesium oxide, and magnesium sulfate. Conjugated estrogens may also interact with maprotiline, potentially decreasing the effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and adverse effects. Monitoring is recommended. Conjugated estrogens increase maravoric levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase toxicity risks, requiring caution and monitoring. Marijuana can also increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating close monitoring. Meropenem decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Meropenem/vaborbactam has a similar effect. Conjugated estrogens may reduce the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring close monitoring. Methylprednisolone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Metronidazole can both increase and decrease the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and altering intestinal flora, respectively. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Conjugated estrogens may reduce metyrapone's effects through an unspecified mechanism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Miconazole vaginally increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Mifepristone also increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating close monitoring. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Mycophenolate may reduce the effects of conjugated estrogens through an unknown mechanism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Neomycin PO decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating close monitoring. Nicardipine increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, requiring caution and monitoring. Nifedipine can both increase and decrease the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, respectively. Monitoring is recommended. Nilotinib increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, necessitating caution and monitoring. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Conjugated estrogens may interact with nortriptyline, potentially decreasing the effects of TCAs while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and adverse effects. Monitoring is recommended. Ofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Ospemifene and conjugated estrogens are contraindicated due to pharmacodynamic synergism, which increases their effects. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Oxytetracycline decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Conjugated estrogens decrease pacritinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism, and alternative drugs should be used. Paromomycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Conjugated estrogens reduce phenindione's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, requiring caution and monitoring. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. If estrogen is used for contraception, loss of contraceptive efficacy may occur. Phytoestrogens may reduce the effects of conjugated estrogens through pharmacodynamic antagonism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Pleurisy root may reduce the effects of conjugated estrogens through an unspecified mechanism, though the interaction is theoretical. Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting OAT3, which may increase adverse effects. Monitoring and dosage adjustments are recommended. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Natural progesterone and conjugated estrogens may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing breast tenderness. Conjugated estrogens reduce protamine's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated.
